question: Define percentage yield and atom economy.
answer: Percentage yield is the actual amount of product divided by the theoretical amount, multiplied by 100; atom economy is the mass of desired product divided by the total mass of products, multiplied by 100
mark_scheme: MP1 1 mark: Yield: actual divided by theoretical times 100. Accept: actual divided by theoretical; actual over theoretical; actual amount divided by theoretical amount; actual yield divided by theoretical yield; actual divided by maximum; actual mass divided by theoretical mass. MP2 1 mark: Atom economy: mass of desired product divided by total mass of products. Accept: mass of desired product divided by total mass of products; mass of desired product over total mass of products; desired product divided by total products; desired product over total products; desired product divided by all products; mass of useful product divided by total mass. Allow any wording that conveys the idea, including common alternatives, correct hedged answers ('I think ...') and clearly intended spelling. Ignore extra correct detail. No mark if the idea is negated, contradicted, or the response gives two different answers.
model_answer: Percentage yield compares the amount of product actually obtained with the maximum theoretical amount, and atom economy is the relative molecular mass of the desired product as a percentage of the sum of the relative masses of all the products.
common_misconceptions: Students swap the definitions.
